Diagnosis: Lymph Node, Left Cervical, Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis
Type.
Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass,' is an encapsulated lymph node
measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance.
Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal
architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis.
Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes,
eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including
classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells
have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD30: Positive
CD15: Positive
PAX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+,
PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical
correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.

node

STOMACH, PARTIAL GASTRECTOMY;
GASTROINTESTINAL STROMAL TUMOR (GIST), SPINDLE CELL TYPE.
Tumor size: 6.5 cm
Mitotic rate: 8 mitoses per 5 mm²
Risk of Progression: High
Surgical margins are negative for tumor.
Microscopic Description:
Sections show a well-circumscribed but encapsulated tumor composed of intersecting fascicles of
sections show a well-circumscribed but encapsulated tumor composed of intersecting fascicles of
unifrom spindle cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and ovoid nuclei. There is mild to moderate nuclear
atypia. The mitotic activity is brisk, counting up to 8 mitoses per 5 mm². Necrosis is not identified.
Gross Description:
Received fresh, labeled with patient's name and "partial gastrectomy," is a 12.0 x 8.0 x 5.0 cm portion
of stomach arising from the gastric wall is a well-circumscribed, fleshy, tan-white submucosal mass
measuring 6.5 x 5.8 x 5.5 cm. The tumor is 0.4 cm from the nearest surgical margin. The overlying
mucosal is intact.
Comments:
The combination of tumor size (6.5 cm) and high mitotic rate (8.5 mitoses per 5 mm²) places his Gastrointestinal
Stomach Tumor (GIST) in the high-risk category for progressive disease. Immunohistochemical studies
confirm the diagnosis, and molecular testing results are pending.

Immunohistochemistry:

Immediate Post-Procedure Care
Transposition: You must be discharged into the care of a responsible adult who will drive you, or use public transportation. A responsible adult must stay with you for the rest of the day. For your safety, it is essential that you carefully follow these instructions.
For the rest of today, begin by drinking clear liquids (such as water, apple juice, ginger ale, or broth) once you are awake.
If you tolerate clear liquids well, you may advance to a light meal a few hours later. Good choices include soup, toast, crackers, or yogurt.

Impressions:
Normal Colonoscopy. The entire colon, from the cecum to the rectum, was visualized and appeared normal. There were no polyps, masses, diverticula, or evidence of inflammation.
Activity: You may feel tired and bloated for the rest of the day. It is important to rest. Do not drive, operate machinery, or make any important decisions for at least 24 hours. You must have a responsible adult stay with you for the remainder of the day. You may resume normal activities tomorrow.
Diet: You may resume your normal diet as tolerated. Start with clear liquids and light foods (e.g., soup, gelatin, crackers) and advance to a regular diet if you are not experiencing nausea or significant bloating. Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods for the first 24 hours.
Follow-up: Based on the normal findings of your colonoscopy, your next routine screening colonoscopy is recommended in 10 years. We will send a reminder to you at that time. If you experience any severe abdominal pain, persistent nausea or vomiting, fever, or significant rectal bleeding, please contact our office immediately or go to the nearest emergency room.
